messages:
alice: Observed sustained etcd WAL fsync tail spikes in us-west-2 around 11:02 UTC; controller-manager lost leader multiple times and GPU onboarding stalled (pods Pending). Falling back to hosted pools caused noticeable cost hit.

infra-bot: [ALERT] etcd_disk_wal_fsync_duration_seconds p99=3.1s (us-west-2)

ryan: Any hardware changes? NVMe firmware updates, host agent updates?

alice: We pushed an nvme firmware batch to the cp NVMe fleet last night. Correlates perfectly: hosts with the new fw show p99 fsync >> 2s. Controller-manager logs show lease renew timeouts: 

```
E0615 11:02:11.012 leaderelection.go:243] failed to renew lease: timed out waiting for the condition
E0615 11:02:11.013 controller_manager.go:184] leader election lost: etcdserver: request timed out
```

ryan: So likely firmware regression causing queue-stalls on fsync path -> WAL tail latency up -> RPCs to etcd slow -> leader renew failures. That will stall leader-only controllers (like nodeclaim), leaving GPU pods Pending.

deepa: Snapshot of provisioning backlog at 11:05: 
```
$ kubectl get pods -n gpu-onboard -o wide
gpu-onboard-0   0/1 Pending  12m
gpu-onboard-1   1/1 Running  47m
```

ryan: Fast mitigations we executed: 1) rolled back firmware on 3 controlplane hosts to previous NVMe FW, 2) cordoned the 2 hottest hosts and restarted controller-manager there, 3) temporarily increased leaderElection leaseDuration to 70s in prod for eu-west/us-west while we validated rollback.

alice: After rollback leader stabilized in ~90s and reconciliation resumed; most Pending GPU pods scheduled within 6m.

deepa: Cost impact: during the ~28m degradation we estimate ~180k tokens went to hosted fallback, approximate incremental cost $540. Finance needs the incident chargeback note.

ryan: Longer-term actions: 1) add a preflight for NVMe FW that runs a small fsync microbenchmark on a canary host and watches etcd WAL fsync p99 before wide rollout, 2) add an alert: etcd WAL fsync p99 > 1s for 2m -> page controlplane owners (current threshold too high), 3) instrument controller-manager with consecutive_lease_renew_failures metric and a small automated mitigation (pause non-critical heavy IO jobs).

alice: Runbook snippet I'll add: detection commands, rollback steps, and a cost-calc line. Quick detection commands I used: 
```
# check leases
kubectl -n kube-system get lease -o wide | grep controller-manager
# etcd p99
curl -s "http://prometheus/api/v1/query?query=histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(etcd_disk_wal_fsync_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))" | jq -r .data.result
# list hosts with new nvme fw
ssh ops@inventory "cat /sys/block/nvme0/device/firmware_rev"
```

infra-bot: incident-created: INC-20260615-210 (severity: medium). Runbook link: https://intranet.redwood/runbooks/nvme-fw-fsync-regression

alice: Assigned follow-ups: alice -> draft runbook + incident timeline; ryan -> automate fw preflight and create canary job; deepa -> cost attach for finance + test leaseDuration in staging. Will report back after canary tests. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
